findings.title: Crash handler passes Node's listener arguments into handleError's exit code
findings.description: `process.on('uncaughtException', handleError)` and `process.on('unhandledRejection', handleError)` hand the listener's second argument to `handleError`. Node passes an origin string for `uncaughtException` and the promise for `unhandledRejection`. Before this diff `handleError` took one parameter, so the extra argument was ignored. The diff adds `exitCode = 1` as that second parameter (errors.ts:46), and it flows into `process.exit(exitCode)` (errors.ts:71). The intended exit code 1 is lost. I could not execute Node here, so the exact result depends on the version. On Node 18, which is the `engines` floor (packages/cli/package.json:37), the value is likely coerced to 0, so a crash could exit successfully. On Node 20+, the exit-code validation probably throws inside the handler. Either way, the crash path no longer exits 1. The existing `errors.test.ts` only covers the default code, and nothing tests the new parameter or the listener wiring. Fix: wrap the listeners, e.g. `process.on('uncaughtException', (err) => handleError(err))`, and add a test for a non-default code.

findings.title: `cf validate frontmatter` ignores worktree scope; `--fix` can write to the main checkout
findings.description:
`validateFrontmatterAction` destructures only `id` from `resolveProjectWorktree`, which drops `worktreeId` and `source: 'worktree'`. It then validates `project.projectPath`, the main checkout. Core's `applyWorktreeOverlay` replaces `projectPath` with `worktreePath` (core `utils/worktree-overlay.ts:9`). `cf check` validates through those overlays (check.ts:220-223), and the other file-touching commands resolve the root with `resolveOperationPath` (utils/worktree-overlay.ts:16-25; used in task.ts:50, slice.ts:36, status.ts:53). Two consequences follow:
- Run from inside a registered worktree, the command validates the main checkout. With `--fix` it rewrites files there, with no confirmation prompt.
- Explicit paths are resolved against the cwd (frontmatterFileValidator.ts:58). A worktree path then fails the containment check against the main root (lines 59-60) and is silently skipped. The command reports "0 files checked" and exits 0.

Fix: derive the root with `resolveOperationPath(project, worktreeId)` and pass that to the validator. Add a test with a worktree-scoped project. No test covers this path today.

findings.title: `--fix` output reports pre-fix totals and never reports how many remain
findings.description: With `--fix`, `findings`, `totalFindings`, `errors`, and `warnings` are all computed from the pre-fix list. The `remaining` list is used only for the exit code (line 154). The JSON payload therefore lists already-fixed findings as findings, and it has no `remaining` or `unfixed` count. A script that reads `totalFindings` or `findings.length` after `--fix` sees failures that were repaired. The human summary has the same gap: "N findings across M files" followed by "Fixed X of N" (lines 74-78), with no unresolved count. The `--json in fix mode` test checks `fixed`, `fixLog`, and `fixErrors` but not the totals. Fix: add a `remaining` count and compute the lists and counts from the post-fix state, or keep the pre-fix counts in a separately named field.

findings.title: Fix application duplicates `ConsistencyChecker.applyFixes`, and the action function is about 70 lines
findings.description: The `--fix` loop (lines 109-134) reimplements an existing path. Core Rule 12 turns the same `validateFrontmatter` findings into fixable items (core ConsistencyChecker.ts:1148-1166). `applyFixes` applies them through `updateFrontmatterField` with a date stamp that defaults to `formatDateProject()` (ConsistencyChecker.ts:210-233). `validate.ts` builds its own `fixLog`/`fixErrors` and makes its own `formatDateProject()` call. That leaves two copies of "apply a frontmatter fix and stamp `dateUpdated`" to drift apart. The action function is roughly 70 lines against the project's ~50-line guideline. Fix: extract an `applyFrontmatterFixes(findings, dateStamp)` helper, ideally in core beside `validateFrontmatterFiles`, and have both commands call it. At minimum, split the fix block out of the action. The validate-and-parse loop duplicated in ConsistencyChecker `ruleFrontmatterSchema` predates this diff, and the comment at ConsistencyChecker.ts:1119-1130 acknowledges it, so I am not counting it against this change.

findings.title: Severity handling is loosely typed and uses scattered string literals
findings.description: `SEVERITY_ICON` is typed `Record<string, string>` and read with `?? '?'` (line 62). The core type is `severity: 'warning' | 'error'` (core frontmatterSchema.ts:25). Typing the map as `Record<FrontmatterFinding['severity'], string>` would let the compiler enforce coverage, and the fallback would no longer be needed. The `?? '?'` is a silent fallback, which CLAUDE.md prohibits, and it cannot fire under the union type anyway. The literals `'error'` and `'warning'` are also compared inline at validate.ts:63 and 140-141, which conflicts with the "define once" rule. `check.ts:25-29` and `check.ts:74-75` repeat the same icon map, the same fallback, and the same colour ternary. A single helper for severity presentation would remove both duplicates.

findings.title: Explicit path arguments that don't resolve are dropped silently and reported as success
findings.description: `cf validate frontmatter typo.md` exits 0 with "No inconsistencies found (0 files checked)". The resolver skips nonexistent, non-`.md`, and out-of-root entries without recording them (core frontmatterFileValidator.ts:52-66). The help text documents this for staged-file lists, where deletions are expected, and skipping deleted files is reasonable. The problem is that a mistyped path looks identical to a clean run, and CLAUDE.md says to fail explicitly rather than fall back silently. Fix: keep the skip behaviour, but return the skipped entries with reasons (for example a `skipped` array in JSON, plus a human-readable line), so a script can tell "nothing to check" from "your path was wrong". Do not change the exit code for deletion-only lists.

findings.title: Misnamed test that cannot detect a regression in the docType constraint
findings.description: The test is titled "a wrong docType literal is still caught by the value-constraint logic", but it asserts zero findings in all three cases, so nothing is caught. Its comments say it proves the docType `values` constraint is enforced. It doesn't. The schema is selected by `FRONTMATTER_SCHEMAS[data.docType]` (frontmatterSchema.ts:228), so the docType values check in step 4 (lines 268-298) can never fail. The docType `values` entries on the schemas are therefore redundant, and the test would still pass if they were deleted. Fix: rename the test and its comments to describe what is asserted (unknown docTypes pass through, and each schema validates only its own docType). Then either drop the redundant docType `values` entries or add a test that exercises them. The positive tests at lines 329-369 do cover the new schemas' required fields.

findings.title: The help text's contrast with `cf check --fix` only partly holds
findings.description: The help says `cf check --fix` asks for confirmation. That is true for the all-slices path (check.ts:243-251). `cf check --fix --slice N` applies fixes with no prompt (check.ts:227-232). Reword the comparison to name the all-slices path, or remove it.

findings.title: The exit-code contract for scripts is not documented
findings.description: The command is described as meant for scripts, but the help text does not state the exit codes. Those codes are 0 for clean, 1 for findings remaining or fix errors, and 2 for a command that could not run, via `handleError(err, 2)`. Other commands use 1 for errors (check.ts:268), so exit 2 here is a different convention. Document the contract in the description or the command reference.

findings.title: Spies are never restored in validate.test.ts
findings.description: `beforeEach` replaces `console.log`, `console.error`, and `process.stdout.write`, and the "exits 2" test replaces `process.exit`. There is no `afterEach(() => vi.restoreAllMocks())`. `vi.clearAllMocks()` clears call history but keeps the implementations, so `process.exit` stays mocked for the rest of the file. `errors.test.ts` and `project.test.ts` do restore their mocks. The leak is harmless today but makes results depend on test order. Add the afterEach.

findings.title: The `dateUpdated` exemption is consistent with the backfill it guards against
findings.description: The comment's claim holds. The `dateUpdated` backfill at frontmatterSchema.ts:243-244 copies `dateCreated` only for fields the schema lists, and the loop at line 233 iterates `schema.fields`. Because the three new schemas omit `dateUpdated`, the backfill never runs for them. The "validates clean without dateUpdated" tests at frontmatterSchema.test.ts:335-369 cover this.
